topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer and situates cancer causation within the course while setting out the lecture's learning objectives.

topics.label: Mutation accumulation and the biological basis of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arise and enable clonal evolution toward cancer within a permissive biological environment.

topics.label: Environmental contributions to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine evidence for environmental contributions to cancer and how those contributions should be understood alongside chance and inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, developing Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example of infection-dependent carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Mechanisms of carcinogen-induced DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage and mutations, showing how biological processing can determine their effects.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutation-inducing initiation from the promotional conditions that allow initiated cells to proliferate into tumours.

topics.label: Developmental susceptibility and carcinogen specificity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the biological context of exposure determines susceptibility to carcinogens and recap the preceding mechanisms in that context.

topics.label: Evidence and methods for assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence linking exposures to cancer is obtained and the limitations of using that evidence to establish carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and framing their practical significance as decisions about risks and benefits.
